newsitem.title: UK: Burmah long-term prospects dispel stg gloom.
newsitem.headline: Burmah long-term prospects dispel stg gloom.

text.p: The strong pound is putting the brakes on Burmah Castrol's near-term profit growth, but underlying business is motoring comfortably ahead and should dispel any currency gloom, analysts said.

In its 1996 results release, lubricants maker Burmah warned this year's earnings might be hit hard if the pound stays at its current strong levels, but the comments merely confirmed what the market already knew, analysts added.
After they had trimmed their earnings forecasts back in January, industry watchers believe now is the time to focus on the group's shining long-term prospects.
"Hopefully we can now bury the currency uncertainty story and get back and look at the underlying growth," said Kleinwort Benson analyst Paul Spedding.

Burmah, which reported a 10 percent increase in 1996 earnings, will benefit in the longer term from the restructuring of its chemical business and a strong presence in booming lubricants markets in Asia and Latin America.
While analysts generally see flat profits in 1997, they expect results to grow by around 10 percent in following years.
"The currency is a short-term hit, but long term you'll absorb it and if you focus on the underlying business you are looking at a very solid operation," said Irene Himona at SocGen.
Burmah's shares, meanwhile, added 18 pence to 1,015-1/2 after having suffered badly earlier in the year when analysts revised their profit estimates.
The 1996 results were higher than they had expected, but this was due to one-off tax benefits which failed to prompt a new round of profit forecast adjustments.
